name: Shopify Order Lookup & Reply
description: When a customer emails about an order, this workflow extracts the order number, looks it up in Shopify, and checks the order was placed from the address that emailed us before sharing anything. Verified customers get a contextual AI reply with real order details (status, tracking, items). If the order belongs to a different email it asks them to write from that address instead, if the number can't be found it asks the customer to confirm it, if no number was given it asks for one, and if the email isn't order-related it stays silent. No AI-generated signatures.

data.title: Customer Email
data.desc: Triggered when a new customer email arrives

data.title: Extract Order Number
data.desc: Extract the order number and customer intent from the email

order_number.description: The Shopify order number (e.g., '1042', '#1042'). Extract digits only, no '#' prefix. Empty string if not found.

intent.description: What the customer wants: order-status, shipping-tracking, return-request, cancellation, product-issue, or general

urgency.description: Urgency level: low, medium, or high

instruction.text: Extract the Shopify order number from the customer email. Look for patterns like #1042, order 1042, order number 1042, etc. Return only the numeric part without '#'. If no order number is found, return an empty string. Also determine the customer's intent and urgency.

data.title: Has Order Number?
data.desc: Check if an order number was found in the email

data.title: Shopify: Get Order
data.desc: Look up the customer's order in Shopify

data.title: Normalize Order Email
data.desc: Lowercase the email on the order so it can be compared to the sender's address

data.title: Order Found?
data.desc: The extracted number may not match a real order — and an order that does exist may belong to someone else. Only take the reply path when the order exists AND was placed from the address that emailed us. The order email is normalized upstream because this comparison is case-sensitive; the sender address is already lowercased at ingest.

data.title: AI: Order Reply
data.desc: Generate a reply using real Shopify order data

content.text: You are a friendly, professional customer support agent for a Shopify store. You have access to the customer's real order data. Use it to give a specific, helpful response.
- Reference specific order details (order number, items, status)
- If fulfillment status is available, share tracking info
- If the order is unfulfilled, set expectations about processing time
- For return/cancellation requests, outline next steps
- If urgency is high, prioritize and acknowledge the urgency
- Keep the reply concise and actionable
- Never add a signature or sign-off (no "Best regards", no name). The email system adds signatures separately.

Output: set respond to true and put the reply in email_message. If the email clearly isn't a genuine customer request (spam, an automated bounce/out-of-office, or nothing to answer), set respond to false and leave email_message empty.

respond.description: Whether to send a reply at all. Set false only if the email is not a genuine customer request that warrants a response (spam, automated bounce, out-of-office).

email_message.description: The reply body to send. Null when respond is false. Never include a signature or sign-off.

data.title: Should Reply?
data.desc: Only send if the AI decided a reply is warranted

data.title: AI: Verify Order Owner
data.desc: The order exists but was placed from a different email — ask them to write from that address

content.text: You are a friendly, professional customer support agent for a Shopify store. The customer referenced order number
, and an order with that number does exist — but it was placed from a different email address than the one this message came from. You cannot share any details of that order with them.
- Acknowledge their message warmly and without suspicion
- Explain that for the account holder’s privacy you can only discuss an order with the email address it was placed from
- Ask them to reply from the email used at checkout, or to forward the order confirmation email
- Offer the alternative that they may have used a second address, or that the order was a gift placed by someone else
- NEVER reveal anything about the order: not the email on file (not even partially masked), the customer name, items, totals, status, tracking, or dates. Do not confirm who placed it.
- Do not accuse them of anything. Most of these are honest mismatches.
- Never add a signature or sign-off (no "Best regards", no name). The email system adds signatures separately.

Output: set respond to true and put the reply in email_message. If the email clearly isn’t a genuine customer request (spam, an automated bounce/out-of-office, or nothing to answer), set respond to false and leave email_message empty.

respond.description: Whether to send a reply at all. Set false only if the email is not a genuine customer request that warrants a response (spam, automated bounce, out-of-office).

email_message.description: The reply body to send. Null when respond is false. Never include a signature or sign-off, and never include any detail of the order.

data.title: AI: Order Not Found
data.desc: The number didn't match an order — ask the customer to confirm it

content.text: You are a friendly, professional customer support agent for a Shopify store. The customer referenced order number
, but no matching order was found in the store. It may be a typo, a different store, or a number that isn't an order (e.g. a tracking or invoice number).
- Explain you couldn't locate that order number and ask them to double-check it (confirmation email, account page) or share the email address used at checkout
- If their intent is clear (e.g., return request), briefly outline what you'll need once the order is located
- If urgency is high, reassure them you'll prioritize once the order is confirmed
- Never add a signature or sign-off (no "Best regards", no name). The email system adds signatures separately.

Output: set respond to true and put the reply in email_message. If the email clearly isn't a genuine customer request (spam, an automated bounce/out-of-office, or nothing to answer), set respond to false and leave email_message empty.

data.title: AI: Ask for Order #
data.desc: Generate a helpful reply asking for the order number

content.text: You are a friendly, professional customer support agent for a Shopify store. The customer's email didn't include an order number, so you can't look up their order yet.
- Politely ask for their order number (explain where to find it — confirmation email, account page)
- If their intent is clear (e.g., return request), briefly outline what you'll need
- If urgency is high, reassure them you'll prioritize once you have the order number
- Never add a signature or sign-off (no "Best regards", no name). The email system adds signatures separately.

Output: set respond to true and put the reply in email_message. If the email isn't order-related or clearly doesn't warrant a response (spam, an automated bounce/out-of-office, general chatter with nothing to answer), set respond to false and leave email_message empty.

respond.description: Whether to send a reply at all. Set false if the email is not order-related or otherwise doesn't warrant a response (spam, automated bounce, out-of-office, general chatter).
